raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Depends on #8017 (which contains #6259), #8023, #8044 and #8049 (which contains #6293). Please review the diff from their merge: [scoped diff](https://github.com/Connor-XY/Megatron-LM/compare/7577c442db...yx/pstate-c6-ckpt-helper-fallbacks).
- The fallbacks use `resolve_process_groups` and `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning` from #8049, and `warn_global_process_group_fallback` from #6293.
- #8044 adds the `dp_cp_group` argument of `ensure_metadata_has_dp_cp_group`. This PR rewrites the fallbacks that #8044 added in `module.py`, `transformer/utils.py` and `core/utils.py`.
- #8023 adds the `FusedMLASelfAttention` metadata call that this PR changes.
- The new tests use #8017's `forbid_global_process_groups` and `new_group_with_same_ranks`.
- Before the sync with main, only the process-group allowlist conflicted in the merges, and the last of those merges regenerated it.

#8057 changes the `process_groups_config` import of `module.py`, and #8035 adds a `pg_collection` argument next to this PR's `gtp_replica_group` in the TE linears. Whichever lands second keeps both sides.

Land this after #8748. Until then MLA, absorbed MLA and GDN build their Transformer Engine linears with only their TP group, so stock training with GTP weight remat would warn once per TE class while the model is built.

**Why.** The checkpoint helpers filled in the global TP and DP×CP groups whenever the caller omitted them, with no warning:
- `make_tp_sharded_tensor_for_checkpoint`, `make_sharded_tensor_for_checkpoint` and `make_sharded_tensors_for_checkpoint`;
- `make_sharded_object_for_checkpoint` without `replica_id`;
- `ensure_metadata_has_dp_cp_group` without a group in the metadata or its argument;
- `MegatronModule.sharded_state_dict` and Mamba's `ExtendedRMSNorm`, for a module without `tp_group`.

Several owners also left out groups they hold. Transformer Engine layers with GTP weight remat left the replica group of their shards to a global lookup at save time. On a model built on its own grid, replica ids then span another grid's ranks, so several ranks or none write a shard.

**What.**
- Each helper fallback emits a `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning` (deprecated in 0.21, removed in 0.23) and selects the same groups as before: the TP group and the GTP-inclusive DP×CP group, through `resolve_process_groups`. The replica-id fallback keeps the rank accessors, so ranks set with `set_tensor_model_parallel_rank()` and `set_data_parallel_rank()` still apply. The metadata warning names the function that called the helper.
- `MegatronModule.sharded_state_dict` takes its collection's `tp` when it has no `tp_group`. A module with no state of its own, such as a data-parallel wrapper, reads no TP group.
- Owners pass their groups:
  - `BertLMHead` takes a `tp_group`, which `BertModel` passes;
  - both mHC layers give their `HyperConnectionModule`s the layer's TP group;
  - the ViT, Qwen VL and Kimi vision encoders keep their decoder's TP group for the weights outside the decoder;
  - `FusedMLASelfAttention` fills missing metadata with its collection's DP×CP group;
  - the InternViT example passes the groups explicitly.
- `TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear`, `TEColumnParallelLinear`, `TERowParallelLinear` and `TEGroupedLinear` read the replica group of their GTP shards (`dp_cp`, or `expt_dp` for experts) from their collection with `vars()`, also through a `MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection`. A layer with GTP shards and no such group warns while it is built and keeps the existing fallback in `gtp_replica_rank`. Nothing reads the global grid at construction.
- The `ValueError` for a `tp_group` passed without its `dp_cp_group` asks for the missing group.
- The allowlist goes from 172 counted reads to 170: eight accessor reads become six guarded ones.

**Tests.** New `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_checkpoint_helper_group_fallbacks.py` runs at TP=2 and skips on an odd number of ranks.
- Passed groups are communicators with the global groups' ranks but distinct from them, and every global accessor and the collection shim raise. No fallback warning may appear. This covers the helpers, `MegatronModule` with a collection and as a stateless container, `ExtendedRMSNorm` and the owners above.
- Omitted groups emit one warning that names the owner and argument, and give the same groups, ranks and shard ids as passing the global groups.
- `_gtp_replica_group` uses the collection's field, also through a multi-module collection. A missing field, an explicit `None` or a missing collection warns and returns `None` without a global read. A layer without GTP needs no group.
- `test_sharded_state_dict_dp_cp_group.py` forbids the global DP×CP group where the fallback reads it.

The new file imports `_gtp_replica_group` at module level, so on main it fails at import instead of showing each test's own failure.

On 4 GPUs against its base, `test_checkpoint_helper_group_fallbacks.py` passes all 19 of its tests, which are new because the base has no such file. `test_sharded_state_dict_dp_cp_group.py` passes 6 tests here and 6 on the base. In the integration run, which merges all #6307 PRs onto main, this PR's test files show no regressions against main: they pass 19 and 6 tests, and main has neither file. With the same changes, end-to-end training smokes on 4 GPUs give bit-identical losses to main and record no process-group fallback warning.

Before the sync with main, the branch ran on 4 CPU gloo ranks with no regressions. The 3 new `_gtp_replica_group` tests pass there, and the other 9 new tests need CUDA.

**Compatibility.**
- On the standard grid the fallbacks select the same groups, so replica ids and checkpoints do not change.
- Changes beyond the warnings:
  - An explicit `dp_cp=None` or `expt_dp=None` on a TE layer with GTP shards now warns. It used to reach the silent fallback at save time.
  - A `MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection`'s language-model group is now stamped on all four TE layers. Such a layer used to get no group and fall back at save time.
  - With `parallel_state` uninitialized, the TP fallback of `MegatronModule` and `ExtendedRMSNorm` gets `None` from the collection shim. It then uses TP=1 replica ids with a warning, where main asserted, and `ExtendedRMSNorm` caches that `None`.
  - InternViT's q/k norm, called directly without metadata, warns and uses the global DP×CP group.
- GTP unit tests that build TE GTP layers from partial collections, such as `required_pgs=['tp', 'cp', 'gtp_remat']`, emit at most one construction warning per TE class. Adding `dp_cp` or `expt_dp` to those collections would silence them without changing behavior.
- Still warn at `torch_dist` save, because their owners hold no groups for them: `FlextronRouter` and the MIMO Hugging Face encoder wrappers.
- Not covered: `InferenceLinear` passes `gtp_remat_group` to `TELinear` without a replica group, so its GTP shards still take the silent fallback in `gtp_replica_rank`. `BertLMHead`'s docstring says an omitted `tp_group` defaults to the global group without saying that this is deprecated.
- Needs `determinism-exempt`: the kernel coverage check flags `transformer_engine.py`, `mamba_mixer.py`, `multi_latent_attention.py` and `transformer/utils.py`. Only process-group plumbing and warnings change.

Synced with main 77391e71cc on 2026-11-01 by a merge commit that lists each conflict and its resolution, so existing commits and review links stay valid.

+def require_process_groups(
+    pg_collection: ProcessGroupCollection, names: Sequence[str], *, owner: str
+) -> Tuple[Any, ...]:
+    """Return the fields ``names`` of ``pg_collection`` in order, or raise if any is absent.
+
+    A field is present once the caller assigns it, including an explicit ``None``, which means
+    that the axis is off or that this rank is not a member of the group (for example ``embd`` on
+    a middle pipeline stage, or ``gtp_remat`` without GTP). A field that was never assigned also
+    reads as ``None`` through ``ProcessGroupCollection.__getattr__``, so a component cannot tell
+    it apart from an axis that is off; this function treats it as a caller error instead.
+
+    Args:
+        pg_collection: The collection the caller passed.
+        names: Fields that ``owner`` and the modules it builds read.
+        owner: Name of the class or function, used in error messages.
+
+    Returns:
+        The groups, one per name and in the order of ``names``.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: ``pg_collection`` is None, a field is absent, or a field holds
+            ``torch.distributed.GroupMember.NON_GROUP_MEMBER``.
+        TypeError: ``pg_collection`` is a ``MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection``. Its modules
+            have different groups, so the caller selects the module's collection.
+    """
+    if pg_collection is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"{owner} requires a ProcessGroupCollection, got None.")
+    if isinstance(pg_collection, MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection):
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"{owner} requires the ProcessGroupCollection of one module, got a "
+            f"MultiModuleProcessGroupCollection with modules {list(pg_collection.keys())}. "
+            "Pass the collection of the module that owns these groups, for example "
+            "pg_collection.get_language_model_collection()."
+        )
+    groups = vars(pg_collection)
+    missing = [name for name in names if name not in groups]
+    if missing:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{owner} requires pg_collection to set {', '.join(missing)}. Set a field to None "
+            "only when its axis is off or this rank is not a member of the group."

+    new_group, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration([list(r) for r in rank_lists])
+    return new_group
+
+
+def build_test_pg_collection(*, tp=1, pp=1, cp=1, ep=1, expt_tp=None, order="tp-cp-ep-dp-pp"):
+    """Build the ProcessGroupCollection of a standard grid without the parallel_state globals.
+
+    The groups have the same ranks as the ones initialize_model_parallel creates for the same
+    sizes and order, with GTP-remat off and one distributed-optimizer instance. In that
+    configuration the GTP-remat and partial data-parallel fields span the same ranks as the plain
+    groups, so they reuse them: dp_gtp_remat, dp_cp_gtp_remat, intra_dp_cp, expt_dp_gtp_remat,
+    intra_expt_dp and tp_ep_pp_with_egtp_remat. The fields it does not build are set to None
+    explicitly, so no resolver falls back to the global grid for an absent field: hcp, gtp_remat,
+    expt_gtp_remat, inter_dist_opt, dp_cp_ag, expt_dp_ag, and the Gloo groups intra_dp_cp_gloo
+    and intra_expt_dp_gloo, as in a job built without Gloo groups. dynamic_cp and dynamic_tp_cp
+    are empty, as they are without dynamic context parallelism.
+
+    Creating groups is collective: call this on every rank, and release the groups with
+    destroy_test_pg_collection.
+
+    Args:
+        tp, pp, cp, ep: Tensor, pipeline, context and expert parallel sizes.
+        expt_tp: Expert tensor parallel size; defaults to `tp`.
+        order: Rank order, as for initialize_model_parallel.
+    """
+    expt_tp = tp if expt_tp is None else expt_tp
+    world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+    if world_size % (tp * cp * pp) or world_size % (expt_tp * ep * pp):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"world size {world_size} must be divisible by tp*cp*pp ({tp * cp * pp}) "
+            f"and by expt_tp*ep*pp ({expt_tp * ep * pp})"
+        )
+    dims = order.split("-")
+    if sorted(dims) != sorted(["tp", "cp", "ep", "dp", "pp"]):
+        raise ValueError(f"order must arrange tp, cp, ep, dp and pp, got {order!r}")
+    sizes = {
+        "tp": tp,
+        "cp": cp,
+        "dp": world_size // (tp * cp * pp),
+        "pp": pp,
+        "expt_tp": expt_tp,
+        "ep": ep,
+        "expt_dp": world_size // (expt_tp * ep * pp),
+    }
+    # Dense layers have no ep axis and expert layers no cp axis, as in initialize_model_parallel.
+    dense_dims = [dim for dim in dims if dim != "ep"]
+    expert_dims = [{"tp": "expt_tp", "dp": "expt_dp"}.get(dim, dim) for dim in dims if dim != "cp"]
+    grid = HyperCommGrid([sizes[dim] for dim in dense_dims], dense_dims)
+    # The expert layers factor the same ranks differently but share the pipeline groups.
+    grid.register_view(
+        "expert", [sizes[dim] for dim in expert_dims], expert_dims, shared_dims=["pp"]
+    )
+
+    dp = grid.create_pg("dp")
+    dp_cp = grid.create_pg(["cp", "dp"])
+    expt_dp = grid.create_pg("expt_dp", view="expert")
+    tp_ep_pp = grid.create_pg(["expt_tp", "ep", "pp"], view="expert")
+    # Every rank creates every embedding group, in the same order; other ranks get None.
+    pp_rank_lists = grid.get_rank_enum("pp")
+    embd, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(
+        [ps.default_embedding_ranks(ranks) for ranks in pp_rank_lists]
+    )
+    pos_embd, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(
+        [ps.default_position_embedding_ranks(ranks) for ranks in pp_rank_lists]
+    )
+    return ProcessGroupCollection(
+        tp=grid.create_pg("tp"),
+        cp=grid.create_pg("cp"),
+        dynamic_cp={},
+        dynamic_tp_cp={},
+        pp=grid.create_pg("pp"),
+        mp=grid.create_pg(["tp", "pp"]),
+        tp_cp=grid.create_pg(["tp", "cp"]),
+        tp_dp_cp=grid.create_pg(["tp", "cp", "dp"]),
+        dp=dp,
+        dp_gtp_remat=dp,
+        dp_cp=dp_cp,
+        dp_cp_gtp_remat=dp_cp,
+        intra_dp_cp=dp_cp,
+        embd=embd,
+        pos_embd=pos_embd,
+        ep=grid.create_pg("ep", view="expert"),
+        expt_tp=grid.create_pg("expt_tp", view="expert"),
+        tp_ep=grid.create_pg(["expt_tp", "ep"], view="expert"),
+        tp_ep_pp=tp_ep_pp,
+        tp_ep_pp_with_egtp_remat=tp_ep_pp,
+        expt_dp=expt_dp,
+        expt_dp_gtp_remat=expt_dp,
+        intra_expt_dp=expt_dp,
+        intra_dp_cp_gloo=None,
+        intra_expt_dp_gloo=None,
+        intra_dist_opt=grid.create_pg(dense_dims),
+        hcp=None,
+        gtp_remat=None,
+        expt_gtp_remat=None,
+        inter_dist_opt=None,
+        dp_cp_ag=None,
+        expt_dp_ag=None,
+    )
+
+
+def destroy_test_pg_collection(pg_collection):
+    """Destroy this rank's groups of a build_test_pg_collection result; call on every rank."""
+    # Every rank finishes its collectives before any communicator goes away.
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.distributed.barrier()
+    groups = {
+        id(group): group
+        for group in vars(pg_collection).values()
+        if isinstance(group, torch.distributed.ProcessGroup)
+    }
+    for group in groups.values():
+        torch.distributed.destroy_process_group(group)

+"""Checkpoint helpers use their owner's groups; an omitted group falls back with a warning.
+
+Called without groups, the sharded-tensor helpers, ``ensure_metadata_has_dp_cp_group``,
+``MegatronModule.sharded_state_dict`` and Mamba's gated norm use the global tensor-parallel and
+DP x CP groups. A TE layer built without the replica group of its GTP shards leaves the choice of
+each shard's writer to the global grid at checkpoint time. On a model with its own grid, replica
+ids then span another grid's ranks. Each of these fallbacks emits a
+``ProcessGroupFallbackWarning``, and the in-repo owners pass the groups they hold.

+def _fallbacks(record):
+    """Return (owner, argument) for each process-group fallback warning in ``record``."""
+    found = []
+    for warning in record:
+        if not issubclass(warning.category, ProcessGroupFallbackWarning):
+            continue
+        message = str(warning.message)
+        assert VERSIONS in message, message
+        # The warning points at the code that omitted the groups, not at Megatron Core.
+        assert warning.filename == __file__
+        found.append(_FALLBACK_MESSAGE.match(message).groups())
+    return found

+def _forbid_global_grid(patch):
+    """Make the global TP, DP and CP accessors raise, including by-name imports of them."""
+    for name in dir(parallel_state):
+        if not name.startswith(_GLOBAL_GRID_PREFIXES):
+            continue
+        original = getattr(parallel_state, name)
+
+        def forbid(*args, _name=name, **kwargs):
+            raise AssertionError(f"read of the global grid: parallel_state.{_name}")
+
+        for module in list(sys.modules.values()):
+            if getattr(module, "__name__", "").startswith("megatron.") and (
+                getattr(module, "__dict__", {}).get(name) is original
+            ):
+                patch.setattr(module, name, forbid)

+class _CoreAttention(torch.nn.Module):
+    """Unmasked softmax attention for the standard and the absorbed (single latent KV) layout."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, softmax_scale=None, v_channels=None, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.softmax_scale = softmax_scale
+        self.v_channels = v_channels
+
+    def forward(self, query, key, value=None, *args, **kwargs):
+        """query/key/value: [s, b, n, d]; absorbed MLA passes one KV head and no value."""
+        if value is None:
+            value = key[..., : self.v_channels]
+        num_heads = query.size(2)
+        key = key.expand(-1, -1, num_heads, -1).float()
+        value = value.expand(-1, -1, num_heads, -1).float()
+        scores = torch.einsum("sbnd,tbnd->bnst", query.float(), key) * self.softmax_scale
+        output = torch.einsum("bnst,tbnd->sbnd", scores.softmax(dim=-1), value)
+        return output.to(query.dtype).flatten(2)
+

+def _build_attention(variant, pg_collection=None):
+    """Build an MLA variant whose down projections are sharded over TP."""
+    backend = TESpecProvider()
+    config = MLATransformerConfig(
+        num_layers=1,
+        hidden_size=256,
+        num_attention_heads=8,
+        q_lora_rank=None if variant.endswith("no_q_lora") else 128,
+        kv_lora_rank=64,
+        qk_head_dim=32,
+        qk_pos_emb_head_dim=32,
+        v_head_dim=32,
+        rope_type="rope",
+        apply_rope_fusion=False,
+        add_bias_linear=False,
+        bf16=True,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=2,
+        sequence_parallel=True,
+    )
+    shared = dict(
+        linear_q_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+        linear_q_up_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+        linear_kv_up_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+        core_attention=_CoreAttention,
+        linear_proj=backend.row_parallel_linear(),
+        q_layernorm=IdentityOp,
+        kv_layernorm=IdentityOp,
+    )
+    if variant.startswith("absorbed"):
+        attention_cls = AbsorbedMLASelfAttention
+        submodules = AbsorbedMLASelfAttentionSubmodules(
+            linear_q_down_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+            linear_kv_down_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+            **shared,
+        )
+    elif variant == "fused":
+        attention_cls = FusedMLASelfAttention
+        submodules = MLASelfAttentionSubmodules(
+            linear_qkv_down_proj=backend.column_parallel_layer_norm_linear(), **shared
+        )
+    else:
+        attention_cls = MLASelfAttention
+        submodules = MLASelfAttentionSubmodules(
+            linear_q_down_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+            linear_kv_down_proj=backend.column_parallel_linear(),
+            **shared,
+        )
+    return attention_cls(
+        config=config,
+        submodules=submodules,
+        layer_number=1,
+        attn_mask_type=AttnMaskType.causal,
+        pg_collection=pg_collection,
+    ).cuda()

+def _sharding_metadata(sharded_state_dict):
+    """The parts of each sharded entry that place it in the global checkpoint."""
+    return {
+        key: (type(value), value.global_shape, value.global_offset, value.replica_id)
+        for key, value in sharded_state_dict.items()
+        if isinstance(value, (ShardedTensor, ShardedObject))
+    }

+class _ParallelStateWithoutGlobalDpCpGroup:
+    """``parallel_state`` as the collection shim sees it, without the global DP x CP group.
+
+    The shim binds a getter for every field and calls only the requested ones, so the data-parallel
+    getter raises when it is called, and requests for other fields still resolve.

+def forbid_global_dp_cp_group():
+    """Make reads of the global data-parallel group through the collection shim raise.

+    The DP x CP fallbacks of the checkpoint helpers read the group there.

+def shard_ids(sharded_state_dict):

+    return sorted(

+        for entry in nested_values(sharded_state_dict)
+    )

+def _split_conversions(added, removed):
+    """Separate the guarded calls in ``added`` that replace a removed read of the same scope.

+    Returns ``(new, converted)``. ``converted`` holds guarded calls matched one for one with
+    removed accessor or shim reads in the same file and scope; ``new`` holds every other call.

+            scope
